planting.note: Plant container-grown plants in spring in well-drained soil in full sun; Fried Egg is a patented (US PP37,533) 2025 Terra Nova Nurseries introduction with yellow-and-white daisy-form blooms.

directions: Fried Egg is a 2025 Terra Nova Nurseries introduction with a cheerful daisy-form bloom: a deep egg-yolk-yellow, cone-like center surrounded by pure white ray petals, evoking a sunny-side-up egg. The compact, fast-growing mound stays under a foot tall with flower stems reaching about 16 inches, and it blooms continuously from midsummer into fall. Grow in full sun in well-drained soil, allowing it to dry moderately between waterings; the lightly fragrant flowers draw butterflies and make good cut flowers, and the cultivar is protected by US Plant Patent 37,533.
sources: Terra Nova Nurseries plant profile (new for 2025)

common_name: Fringe Festival Coneflower (Fully Double Coneless Pink-Orange-Red Echinacea)

planting.note: Plant container-grown plants in spring in average, well-drained soil in full sun; Fringe Festival is a 2025 Terra Nova Nurseries introduction with fully double, coneless flowers in blended pink, orange, and red tones.

directions: Fringe Festival is a novelty double coneflower with no visible center cone, instead producing dense, shaggy masses of petals in blended shades of pink, orange, and red that the breeder compares to thick shag-carpet texture. The sturdy, medium-tall plant holds deep green, strap-like foliage close to the ground and sends up flower stems to about 16 inches from a base only 8 inches tall. It blooms from midsummer through fall in full sun and average, well-drained soil, and is deer-resistant and attractive to pollinators; as a new Terra Nova release the plant patent is still pending.
sources: Terra Nova Nurseries plant profile (new for 2025)

common_name: Prima Aura Coneflower (Bicolor Rose-Pink and Lime Echinacea)

planting.note: Plant container-grown plants in spring in average, well-drained soil in full sun; Aura is a 2025 Terra Nova Nurseries introduction that opens the new Prima coneflower series, with rose-pink-and-lime bicolor blooms.

directions: Prima Aura opens the Terra Nova Nurseries PRIMA coneflower collection with two-toned blooms combining a rose-pink heart and a pastel lime-green outer ring on stiff, upright stems well suited to cutting. Introduced for 2025, this Echinacea purpurea selection forms a fast-growing, upright clump about 13 inches tall with flowers rising to roughly 19 inches, and tolerates the heat and humidity of Deep South gardens. Grow in full sun in average, well-drained soil, letting it dry moderately between waterings; it is deer-resistant, fragrant, and attracts butterflies and hummingbirds over a long June-through-October bloom season.
sources: Terra Nova Nurseries plant profile (Prima series, new for 2025)

planting.note: Plant container-grown plants in spring in well-drained soil in full sun, avoiding deep planting of the crown; Kiwi is a 2025 Terra Nova Nurseries addition to the compact, early-blooming Kismet coneflower series, with lime-green flowers.

directions: Kismet Kiwi extends Terra Nova's compact, early-flowering Kismet coneflower line with unusual lime-green blooms that the breeder attributes to extra chlorophyll in the petals, giving the flowers exceptional substance and vase life. The clumping plant reaches about 14 inches in foliage height with flower stems to 27 inches, blooming from early summer into fall. Plant in full sun in well-drained soil that is allowed to dry moderately between waterings, taking care not to bury the crown at planting time; it is deer-resistant and draws butterflies and other pollinators, and makes an excellent cut flower.
sources: Terra Nova Nurseries plant profile (Kismet series, new for 2025)

common_name: Princess Citrus Coneflower (Compact Lime-and-Lemon Pot-Culture Echinacea)

planting.note: Plant container-grown plants in spring in average, well-drained soil in full sun; Citrus is a 2025 Terra Nova Nurseries introduction in the new, pot-culture-bred Princess coneflower series.

directions: Princess Citrus belongs to a new Terra Nova series bred specifically for container and pot culture, carrying lime-green and lemon-yellow flowers that develop warm cantaloupe tones at the petal base as the season progresses. The naturally compact, mounding plant stands about 10 inches tall with bloom stems to 17 inches, flowering heavily from early summer through fall. Grow in full sun in average, well-drained soil with moderate watering; it is deer-resistant, fragrant, and attracts hummingbirds and other pollinators, performing equally well as a solo container specimen or mixed into a sunny border.
sources: Terra Nova Nurseries plant profile (Princess series, new for 2025)

common_name: Princess Honey Coneflower (Compact Honey-Orange Pot-Culture Echinacea)

planting.note: Plant container-grown plants in spring in average, well-drained soil in full sun; Honey is a 2025 Terra Nova Nurseries introduction in the new, pot-culture-bred Princess coneflower series.

directions: Princess Honey is a compact, pot-crop-bred coneflower in Terra Nova's new Princess series, bearing rich honey-toned orange-yellow blooms over deep green foliage that reaches almost to the ground for a tidy, tailored look. The fast-growing mound tops out around 10 inches with flower stems to about 15 inches, blooming from early summer into fall. Grow in full sun in average, well-drained soil, allowing it to dry moderately between waterings; the fragrant flowers are especially attractive to butterflies, and the compact habit suits containers as readily as border plantings.
sources: Terra Nova Nurseries plant profile (Princess series, new for 2025)

common_name: Supreme Lime Coneflower (Novelty Green Spider-Form Echinacea)

planting.note: Plant container-grown plants in spring in well-drained, moderately fertile soil in full sun; Lime is a 2025 Terra Nova Nurseries addition to the Supreme coneflower series, with unusual green spider-mum-style blooms.

directions: Supreme Lime adds an unusual green-flowered selection to Terra Nova's Supreme coneflower series, producing spider-mum-style blooms described as the mellow green of melon flesh on tall, strong stems well above the foliage. It forms a vigorous, fast-growing clump about 20 inches tall with flower stems reaching 30 inches, blooming from midsummer through fall and excelling as a cut flower. Grow in full sun in well-drained soil of moderate fertility, letting it dry moderately between waterings; it is deer-resistant and still attracts bees and butterflies despite its novel coloring.
sources: Terra Nova Nurseries plant profile (Supreme series, new for 2025)
